meta.tagline: When the fairytale set turns out real: half-timber, canals and Riesling

pills: Capital of the Alsace Wine Route
Walkable in half a day, savoured in three

overview.title: Welcome to Colmar
overview.intro: Your first steps in Colmar feel like walking onto a film set: candy-coloured half-timbered houses, flower-draped canals, street names left over from the Middle Ages. Then the smell of a bakery hits you, glasses clink in a winstub, and you understand — this is no set, it's a living Alsatian town. French elegance and German order share a table here; on the table, there is Riesling.

local_word.definition: Alsace's wine tavern: wood panelling, checked tablecloths, choucroute steam and local wine by the jug. Warmer than a restaurant, heartier than a bar; a winstub table is the shortest route to understanding Colmar.

rules.title: Be on the streets before 9 am
rules.description: Colmar is small and its fame is big: by day, coach tours fill Little Venice. The town's fairytale self lives in the early morning and early evening — that's when both the photos and the peace are taken.

rules.title: Don't leave the Wine Route unplanned
rules.description: Colmar sits at the very centre of the Alsace Wine Route; Eguisheim and Riquewihr are half an hour away. Car, tour or bicycle — decide how on day one, not on your last day.

rules.title: Mind the Monday–Tuesday closures
rules.description: Museums and many restaurants close on Monday or Tuesday; check the day so you don't leave without seeing the Unterlinden.

tip.label: The Colmar philosophy
tip.text: In this town the list of sights is short and the list of corners to sit in is long. When you find a bench by the canal, pocket the list; Colmar comes to you anyway.

transport.title: Getting Around
transport.intro: Colmar's mode of transport is called shoes; the rest is for leaving town.

items.title: Arriving by train
items.description: About 2.5 hours from Paris by TGV, 30 minutes from Strasbourg, 45 from Basel. The station is a 10-minute walk from the centre; no taxi needed.

items.title: Everywhere on foot
items.description: The historic centre is 20 minutes end to end: Little Venice, the Unterlinden, the old market streets all within strolling range. Cobble-proof shoes are the only requirement.

items.title: The Wine Route by bicycle
items.description: Colmar sits on a plain; the wine villages are 30–60 minutes by bike. Rental shops in the centre, routes signposted — in spring and autumn this is the loveliest way to travel.

items.title: Buses and tours to the villages
items.description: Regional buses reach Eguisheim, Riquewihr and Kaysersberg but run sparsely; wine-tour minibuses with tastings included are a practical alternative.

items.title: Rental car — the free route
items.description: To ride the Wine Route at your own tempo, rent by the station; parking inside the villages is tight, use the main lots. The taster doesn't drive — tastings are serious in Alsace.

callout.label: Little train note
callout.text: The tourist 'petit train' in the centre is sweet, but Colmar is a town made for walking; spend the money on a glass of Grand Cru instead.

stay.title: Where to Stay
stay.intro: In Colmar the distances are small and the differences in atmosphere are big; canal view or vineyard view — your call.

local_word.definition: The French holiday house-guesthouse: in Alsace usually a historic half-timbered building with a flowered courtyard. Friendlier than a hotel, comfortable as home — the classic way to stay in the villages.

items.name: Little Venice (Petite Venise)
items.description: Waking in a canal-side house puts you in Colmar's very heart: geraniums at the window, empty morning lanes. Prices high, rooms few — book early.

items.name: Old Town — around the cathedral
items.description: Around Saint-Martin and the market streets: restaurants, patisseries and museums at your doorstep. Daytime tourist density rises, but the location is beyond argument.

items.name: Around the station
items.description: A calm quarter 10 minutes' walk from the centre: chain hotels and fair prices. A sensible base for Wine Route drivers and train connections.

items.name: Eguisheim — sleeping in a wine village
items.description: The circular medieval village 10 minutes away: when the tourists leave at dusk the village is yours, and you wake to walks in the vines. A sweet alternative to Colmar for those with a car.

items.name: Towards Riquewihr — Wine Route bases
items.description: The gîtes around Riquewihr and Kaysersberg suit a tasting-heavy program: the producers become your neighbours. Colmar is 20–30 minutes away; in the evening your own village's fairytale suffices.

best_time.title: When to Go
best_time.intro: Colmar has two peaks: flowers in summer, lights in winter. The seasons between are the connoisseur's secret.

items.label: Spring
items.name: The Awakening
items.subtitle: Spring · Flowering canals, calm streets
items.description: Geraniums go up in the windows, the first green shows in the vines, the crowds haven't reached summer scale. The airiest window for cycling the Wine Route.

callout.label: May tip
callout.text: In May the wine villages switch to festival mode; if a weekend fête coincides with your trip, change your plans and choose the fête.

items.label: Summer
items.name: Flower Peak
items.subtitle: Summer · Painted façades, full terraces
items.description: The town drowns in flowers, canal boats and terraces run at capacity. The price of the beauty is the crowd: at midday you walk shoulder to shoulder in Little Venice.

callout.label: Midday warning
callout.text: Coach tours fill the town from 10:00 to 16:00; save those hours for museums or the villages, and live the streets at morning and dusk.

items.label: Autumn
items.name: The Harvest
items.subtitle: Autumn · Vendanges, golden vines, new wine
items.description: The vineyards turn gold, harvest festivals begin in the villages, the air smells of grapes. Colmar's most photogenic and most delicious season — those in the know always choose it.

callout.label: October tip
callout.text: In early October, during the vendanges, producers open their doors; new wine with warm onion tart is not to be missed.

items.label: Winter
items.name: The Christmas Tale
items.subtitle: Winter · Christmas markets, lights, mulled wine
items.description: In December Colmar becomes one of Europe's loveliest Christmas markets: five separate squares, light shows, vin chaud steam. January and February are the town at its calmest and most local.

callout.label: December note
callout.text: Christmas market season pushes hotel prices past the summer peak; a December plan needs booking two or three months ahead.

eat.title: What to Eat
eat.intro: Alsatian cooking is the marriage of French technique and German appetite; Colmar is that marriage's kitchen.

local_word.definition: The Alsace classic of fermented cabbage crowned with sausages and cuts of meat: it looks heavy and lightens with Riesling. Eat it properly once, in a winstub — after that it's a memory.

items.name: Tarte flambée (flammekueche)
items.description: Cream, onion and bacon on paper-thin dough: Alsace's 'pizza' comes out of the wood oven in seconds and is shared by hand. Beer works, so does Riesling.

items.name: Bretzel and kugelhopf
items.description: The icons of the bakery window: the glossy salted bretzel and the sweet almond-apricot kugelhopf. One of them beside your morning coffee — both if undecided.
items.tag: From the bakery · fresh in the morning

items.name: Choucroute garnie
items.description: Fermented cabbage, three kinds of sausage, smoked meats: the monument of the Alsatian table. Portions are serious; sharing is not shameful, it is wise.

items.name: Munster cheese
items.description: The washed-rind cheese from the valley: its smell demands courage, its taste repays it. Served with cumin; a legendary match with Gewurztraminer.
items.tag: For the brave · try it with cumin

items.name: Alsace whites — Riesling to Gewurz
items.description: Riesling, Pinot Gris, Gewurztraminer, Crémant: in the capital of the Wine Route, the glasses are in town and the cellars in the villages. Leaving without a tasting does Colmar an injustice.
items.tag: Cellar tastings · ask for Grand Cru

items.name: Tarte aux quetsches — plum tart
items.description: The Alsatian tart of purple damsons in season: light on sugar, heavy on fruit, pure patisserie classic. If you've come in late summer, smile at your luck.

callout.label: The winstub rule
callout.text: The marks of a good winstub: a short menu, a French-German mix of language, wine arriving by the jug. Ask for 'Edelzwicker' — an honest Alsatian blend at a friendly price.

hidden_gems.title: Hidden Gems
hidden_gems.intro: Colmar's shop window belongs to everyone; these six corners belong to early risers and corner-turners.

items.rarity: A quiet giant of world art
items.name: Unterlinden Museum — the Isenheim Altarpiece
items.description: At the heart of the museum, set in an old convent, stands Grünewald's Isenheim Altarpiece: the most shattering work of the Northern Renaissance. None of the Louvre's crowds, several times the impact.

items.name: Bartholdi Museum
items.description: Auguste Bartholdi, creator of the Statue of Liberty, was a Colmar man; his birth house is now a museum. A courtyard full of models of New York's icon — the town's sweetest surprise.

items.name: Maison des Têtes
items.description: A mansion from 1609 whose façade is covered with 106 grotesque heads: most visitors pass without looking. Count them slowly from across the street — every one is different.

items.name: Marché Couvert
items.description: The brick market hall of 1865: cheesemongers, charcutiers, tart stalls. Its rear terrace over the canal is lunch's best-kept address.

items.name: Above Eguisheim — the Three Towers
items.description: Just outside Colmar, three ruined medieval keeps on a hill above the vines: a short walk, an endless vineyard view, and solitude at sunset.

items.name: The rooftops of the Tanners' Quarter
items.description: The steep-roofed houses of the tanners' district were built with drying lofts; for those who know the façade colours once coded the old guilds, the town reads like an open book.

callout.label: Morning bonus
callout.text: Little Venice's classic photo spot, the Saint-Pierre bridge, is empty at 8 am — and the light rises exactly there.

traps.title: Skip the Traps
traps.intro: Colmar is a harmless town; its traps cost time rather than fortunes. Know these four and live the fairytale efficiently.

items.name: The midday queue for the canal boats
items.description: Waiting 45 minutes at noon for a very short boat ride is the worst way to spend time in Colmar.
items.instead: Take the first morning boat or skip it entirely: the same canal is lovelier on foot, and free.

items.name: Photo menus on the Little Venice quay
items.description: Some canal-view terraces sell frozen flammekueche at tourist prices; it's the one thing that shadows Alsatian cooking's good name.
items.instead: Walk two streets in: in the locals' winstubs the same dish arrives at half the price with twice the flavour.

items.name: Souvenir 'Alsace dolls' and stork piles
items.description: Mass-produced storks and imported ornaments labelled 'handmade' fill every corner of the old town; space in the suitcase, a hole in the budget.
items.instead: For a real keepsake choose wine from a producer, local pottery (Soufflenheim), or a jar of honey from the market.

items.name: Cramming the Wine Route into one day
items.description: The five-villages-in-a-day 'completion' tour means seeing them all through a bus window; Alsace villages are beautiful in the lingering, not the rushing.
items.instead: Pick two villages (Eguisheim + Riquewihr is the classic) and give each half a day; never hurry a tasting.

callout.label: The golden rule
callout.text: In Colmar the crowd flows one way; walk two streets against it. Ninety percent of the town waits quietly just behind the ten percent in the shop window.

itinerary.title: Ready-Made Routes
itinerary.intro: If you hate planning, follow these flows. The times are flexible; keep the spirit, break the order.

plans.title: If You Have 1 Day
plans.subtitle: Canal, altarpiece and a wine village

steps.title: Little Venice — empty
steps.description: Start from the Saint-Pierre bridge and walk the canal: before the tourists, the town belongs to you and the bakers.

steps.title: Bakery breakfast + old town
steps.description: Coffee with a bretzel or kugelhopf; then a heads-up walk past the façades of the Maison des Têtes and the Pfister House.

steps.title: Unterlinden Museum
steps.description: Give the Isenheim Altarpiece two hours; breathe in the convent courtyard. This is Colmar's one world-class 'must'.

steps.title: Lunch at the Marché Couvert
steps.description: A cheese-and-charcuterie plate or a tart from the market hall; eat on the rear terrace over the canal.

steps.title: Eguisheim escape
steps.description: A 10-minute hop to the circular village: walk its concentric lanes, taste a Riesling at a producer, climb to the Three Towers.

steps.title: Winstub evening
steps.description: Back in Colmar: choucroute or flammekueche under wood panelling, Edelzwicker by the jug. Santé!

plans.title: If You Have 3 Days
plans.subtitle: Live the town as a guest, not a tourist

steps.title: Colmar itself
steps.description: The 1-day flow above: canals at dawn, the Unterlinden, the market hall, a winstub at night.

steps.title: The northern Wine Route
steps.description: Riquewihr's walled lanes, lunch in Ribeauvillé, the climb to the Schlossberg above Kaysersberg; two producer tastings, then a village gîte or the drive back to Colmar.

steps.title: A slow goodbye
steps.description: The Bartholdi Museum and the Tanners' Quarter in the morning, a tarte aux quetsches break at noon, an afternoon cycling the vineyard plain — then to the train or the road, bottles of Riesling aboard.

phrases.title: The 5-Word Survival Kit
phrases.intro: French courtesy is the key here too; a pinch of Alsatian on top guarantees smiles.

items.meaning: Hello — the mandatory first word of every exchange
Please — add it to the end of your order
Cheers! — Riesling glasses rise to this
The all-purpose Alsatian exclamation: 'come on, okay, there we go' — hear it and you're in Alsace

items.sub: From the wood oven, edges charred

items.label: Leave with a kugelhopf mould
items.sub: Or at least a kugelhopf — fresh from the bakery
